subject: MSA + Order Form kickoff — regional deployment carveouts & exhibit ownership
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@securocloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA kickoff and initial redlines (regional residency concerns)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this on. We reviewed Redwood's standard MSA and have two principal asks up front:

1) Data residency carveouts — SecuroCloud will host customer data in multiple regions; for regulatory reasons we need an Exhibit that maps hosting regions to permitted data classes and an explicit carveout for EU-resident PII.

2) Exhibit ownership — we want the Order Form Exhibit A to include a table of regions, services, and residency commitments. We can share a first-draft exhibit (attached) and would like to understand which fields Redwood expects to control versus customer-editable fields.

I attached our annotated draft of the Order Form exhibit and a short redline of your MSA. Can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff with your legal/ops team this week? Availability: Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Asha
Asha Patel
Head of Compliance, SecuroCloud

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the materials and clear asks. Looping in Kimberly (privacy & contracting) and Marissa (contracts ops) to pick this up — Jonas from product will help confirm the hosting surface.

Quick plan:
- Kimberly, can you take the redline first pass and call out any policy blockers or template exceptions (esp. the EU PII carveout)?
- Marissa, please prepare a short exhibit mapping template (doc in Drive) that shows which columns Redwood expects to be static versus negotiable.
- Jonas, can you confirm whether the EU residency commitments can be met via existing region flags or if we need a contractual commitment per-customer?

Asha — we have availability Wed 2:00–3:30pm PT or Thu 9:00–10:00am PT. Which works for you? If Wednesday is preferred we can send a calendar invite and a one-page agenda.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — I reviewed SecuroCloud's redline and the draft exhibit. High-level notes:

- EU PII carveout: we can agree to an Exhibit that enumerates regions and data classes, but the MSA template's liability and data processing clauses will need scoped language. I flagged two clauses that need legal-approved alternative language (Sections 6.2 and 9.1).
- Operational commitment: for some managed features (e.g., guaranteed residency for backups) we may need to convert a technical promise into an order-form level SLA or an appendix.
- Template ownership: Redwood prefers to own Exhibit structure but can allow counterparty edits in defined cells (region, account name, permitted classes). We'll propose a small set of editable fields.

Action items I suggest before the kickoff:
1) Marissa: publish a one-page Exhibit template in Drive that maps control vs editable fields (I can mark the two MSA clauses that require legal sign-off).
2) Vanessa/Jonas: confirm whether the product flags cover backup residency (Jonas, any docs you can drop into the Drive folder will help).
3) Vanessa: confirm kickoff slot with Asha (Wed 2pm PT preferred).

I'll prepare a short redline summary that highlights the policy blockers and a recommended response for each.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
